revision_changelog.r3__OQ1_set_of_writes_fix: RESOLVED (FIX 1 — the ONE residual OQ1 false-positive surviving r2). r2 paired the SharedRead S[r] against ONLY the MOST-RECENT prior SharedWrite of the id, so a CORRECT same-invocation multi-slot kernel that writes TWO of its OWN slots and then reads back the FIRST is FALSE-HARD-ERRORED: `tile[0u32]=a; tile[1u32]=b; let w=tile[0u32];` — here index_relation(most_recent_write=IntLit(1), read=IntLit(0))=ProvablyDisequal -> HARD ERROR, but slot 0 WAS written earlier by THIS invocation (a safe self-RAW, no barrier needed). FIX: track the SET (Vec) of ALL prior same-block SharedWrite index expressions to that id SINCE THE LAST BARRIER (no intervening HirStmt::Barrier, no back-edge/branch), not just the most-recent. REFINED RULE for `SharedRead S[r]`: (1) if `index_relation(w_k, r) == ProvablyEqual` for ANY prior write index `w_k` in the set -> NO diagnostic (the invocation reads a slot it itself wrote — correct self-RAW); (2) else if `index_relation(w_k, r) == ProvablyDisequal` for EVERY prior write index `w_k` in the set -> HARD ERROR SharedMissingBarrierBeforeCrossInvocationRead (provably a slot this invocation never wrote = the genuine cross-invocation trap); (3) else (Unknown vs at least one prior write — i.e. NOT provably equal to any AND NOT provably disequal to all) -> ADVISORY WARNING HirWarning::SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead. This restores ZERO false positives: the multi-slot self-write case `tile[0]=a; tile[1]=b; let w=tile[0];` is now ProvablyEqual-to-a-prior-write (the tile[0]=a write) -> NO diagnostic. Same expr.rs leaf machinery (BindingId Eq / IntLit value / GidBuiltin axis) — the ONLY change is a Vec<index-expr> of prior writes since the last barrier instead of a single Option<most-recent>; a barrier clears the set. Updated: A.4.1 (set-based rule), the typecheck.rs analysis description (item 5), AT-1636 (adds the multi-slot-self-write NO-diagnostic case). The single-invocation `@workgroup(1,1,1)` kernel that writes S[0] and reads an UNwritten S[1] still hard-errors (S[1] is ProvablyDisequal to the ONLY prior write S[0]) — documented as ACCEPTABLE: that is an uninitialized read, buggy regardless of any barrier (a barrier would not make it correct); only the diagnostic NAME is slightly off (it says 'missing barrier' when the true bug is 'uninitialized read'), which is cosmetic, not a soundness hole.

revision_changelog.r2__OQ1_soundness_fix: RESOLVED (the ONE blocking defect from the r1 pessimistic review). The r1 OQ1 hard error (A.4.1) keyed ONLY on the shared-id X — so a CORRECT same-invocation same-index self read-after-write `tile[i]=v; ... =tile[i];` (which needs NO barrier — an invocation always observes its own writes in program order) would be FALSE-POSITIVE rejected, invalidating the explicit zero-false-positive justification for the hard-error severity. CHOSEN OPTION: the SOUND-NARROW HARD ERROR (option 1 of the two offered), NOT warning-only — because the index-disequality predicate IS decidably implementable on the actual HIR (VERIFIED below). NEW PRECISE RULE (A.4.1, fully rewritten): the hard error HirError::SharedMissingBarrierBeforeCrossInvocationRead fires for shared-id X ONLY when, in the SAME basic block with NO intervening HirStmt::Barrier and NO back-edge/branch between them, a SharedWrite `S[w]` is followed by a later SharedRead `S[r]` AND the index expressions `w` and `r` are PROVABLY DISEQUAL (a provable cross-slot access — the genuine cross-invocation trap). When `w` and `r` are PROVABLY EQUAL (same SSA index — identical LocalRead(BindingId) with no reassignment between, same IntLit value, same GidBuiltin axis) -> NO error and NO warning (correct same-invocation self-RAW). When the indices are NEITHER provably equal NOR provably disequal -> ADVISORY WARNING HirWarning::SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead (undecidable). This restores zero false positives: a correct kernel is NEVER hard-errored. IMPLEMENTABILITY VERIFIED against crates/axc-hir/src/expr.rs: HirExprKind index is a Box<HirExpr>; BindingId derives PartialEq/Eq/Hash (expr.rs:20-21) so LocalRead SSA-equality is a BindingId comparison; IntLit carries a comparable `value` (constant disequality = distinct literal values); GidBuiltin carries an `axis` (provable equality by axis). A small structural predicate `index_relation(w, r) -> {ProvablyEqual, ProvablyDisequal, Unknown}` is therefore decidable for exactly these leaf cases and returns Unknown (-> warning) for everything else (Binary/arith index expressions, any LocalRead whose binding was reassigned between the write and the read). Updated: A.4.1 (rewritten), the typecheck.rs change item (key on (id, index-disequality), exclude provably-equal self-reads, demote Unknown to warning), AT-1606 (now also asserts the same-index self-read does NOT hard-error), NEW AT-1636 (the positive zero-false-positive test). The error variant NAME and the advisory warning are unchanged from r1; only the FIRING CONDITION narrows from `same id` to `same id + provable index disequality`.

## M3.2 (r2) Technical Specification — shared[T,N] + competitive matmul + tiled attention (NOT FA2)

### PART A — shared[T,N] workgroup-local memory

#### A.1 Syntax & grammar

Declaration form (body-level statement):
```
@kernel @workgroup(256,1,1)
fn k(out: buffer[f32]) -> void {
    shared tile: shared[f32, 256];   // workgroup-shared array, 256 f32 = 1 KiB
    let lid: u32 = gid(0u32);
    tile[lid] = out[lid];            // SharedWrite
    workgroup_barrier();             // REQUIRED for cross-invocation visibility
    let v: f32 = tile[255u32 - lid]; // SharedRead
    out[lid] = v;
    return;
}
```
- The leading keyword `shared` introduces the declaration (lexer already has TokenKind::Shared). The type is `shared[elem, N]` where `elem` is a ScalarTypeRef and `N` is an **unsuffixed positive integer literal** (anti-pattern #1: NO inference, NO const-expr fold in M3.2 beyond a bare literal).
- Shared arrays are KERNEL-WIDE workgroup storage. Multiple decls allowed (distinct SharedId each). A `shared[T,N]` in parameter position is a hard error (consumes no descriptor).

#### A.2 HIR lowering
1. Parser emits `Stmt::SharedDecl { name, elem, len }` + `TypeRef::Shared(elem,N)`.
2. lower.rs: each SharedDecl -> `SharedDecl { id: SharedId(next), name, ty: SharedTy{elem,len}, span }`. Hard errors: N==0 (SharedZeroLength), N>65536 (SharedTooLarge), elem not in is_allowed_shared_element (SharedElementTypeUnsupported — Bool rejected), duplicate name (SharedDuplicateName), param/binding collision (SharedNameCollision).
3. typecheck resolves `name[i]`->SharedRead (index MUST be U32 — SharedIndexNotU32, no coercion) and `name[i]=v`->SharedWrite (value MUST match elem ScalarTy exactly — SharedWriteTypeMismatch).
4. Aggregate bytes = Σ len*elem_byte_size. Warn > 16384 (Vulkan portable min); hard error > 65536 (SharedMemoryTooLarge).

#### A.3 SPIR-V codegen
emit_shared_globals (BEFORE begin_block, like SSBOs) per decl:
```
%elem    = OpTypeFloat 32                  ; via ScalarTypeCache::scalar_id
%n_const = OpConstant %u32 256             ; array length is an OpConstant ID (SPIR-V 3.32.6), NOT a literal
%arr     = OpTypeArray %elem %n_const      ; SIZED array (not OpTypeRuntimeArray)
%ptr_wg  = OpTypePointer Workgroup %arr
%var     = OpVariable %ptr_wg Workgroup    ; GLOBAL (module-scope) variable, NO initializer
%ptr_e   = OpTypePointer Workgroup %elem   ; Workgroup elem-ptr (cache per elem type; SHARED across distinct arrays of the same elem type)
```
- Workgroup OpVariable has NO initializer (Vulkan forbids it without VK_KHR_zero_initialize_workgroup_memory; rely on write-before-read + barrier discipline). KNOWN SHARP EDGE: reading a cell never written reads garbage; the compiler does not prove every read index was written (undecidable) — documented.
- GLOBAL variables -> NOT in the Function first-block prelude. Emitted in module.types_global_values (same timing as SSBOs).
- SPIR-V 1.3 OpEntryPoint interface: only Input/Output. Workgroup vars EXCLUDED (forward-compat: SPIR-V 1.4+ lists all globals; repo pins 1.3).
- DEDUP: two shared arrays of the SAME elem type SHARE the %ptr_e Workgroup pointer type (cache) but get DISTINCT %arr (OpTypeArray) + %var (OpVariable) ids — even if N is identical (distinct names). The cache must key the OpTypeArray/OpVariable by SharedId, NOT collapse by (elem,N). AT-1615.

Indexed access — SINGLE index:
```
; read tile[i]
%idx = <emit index>            ; u32
%ptr = OpAccessChain %ptr_e %var %idx   ; ONE index (no leading struct-member-0)
%val = OpLoad %elem %ptr
; write tile[i] = v
%ptr = OpAccessChain %ptr_e %var %idx
       OpStore %ptr %v
```
KEY DIFFERENCE vs SSBO: SSBO chain is `%var %0 %index` (struct-member-0 then array index, because buffers.rs wraps the runtime array in OpTypeStruct); shared ARRAY chain is `%var %index` (direct — no wrapping struct). Do NOT copy the SSBO two-index pattern.

#### A.4 Barrier + memory-semantics requirement (CRITICAL correctness)
Cross-invocation read-after-write through shared memory is correct ONLY with a workgroup control barrier carrying WorkgroupMemory semantics between the write and read phases. AXIOM-Compute reuses `workgroup_barrier()` verbatim (VERIFIED subgroup.rs:34,298-300; test asserts scope 2/2 + semantics 0x108 at 517-519):
```
OpControlBarrier %Workgroup(2) %Workgroup(2) %(AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory = 0x108)
```
Execution scope Workgroup(2) => all invocations rendezvous; WorkgroupMemory(0x100) => prior shared writes visible to subsequent shared reads across invocations. No new barrier kind. For the straight-line stage->barrier->read pattern a SINGLE barrier suffices; for the LOOPED matmul TWO barriers per K-iteration are required (write-visibility + WAR-protection before the next iteration overwrites the staging arrays).

#### A.4.1 OQ1 — SOUND missing-barrier analysis (r2): provable CROSS-SLOT = HARD ERROR; provable same-slot self-read = NO diagnostic; undecidable = advisory warning
WHY THE r1 KEY WAS UNSOUND: keying the hard error only on the shared-id X (a SharedWrite of X followed by a SharedRead of X in the same block, no intervening barrier) FALSE-POSITIVES a CORRECT same-invocation, same-index self read-after-write — e.g. `tile[i] = v; ... let w = tile[i];`. That read needs NO barrier: an invocation ALWAYS observes its own prior writes in program order (intra-invocation memory order is sequential). A barrier is required ONLY for a CROSS-invocation read — invocation A reading a slot that a DIFFERENT invocation B wrote. Distinguishing cross- vs same-invocation in general is UNDECIDABLE, so the HARD ERROR is reserved for a narrowly-decidable PROVABLE cross-slot pattern and EXCLUDES provable self-reads.

PRECISE RULE (r3 — track the SET of prior writes, not just the most-recent). Within a SINGLE basic block (no branch, no back-edge between the statements), maintain the SET `W_X` of index expressions of ALL prior SharedWrites of shared-id X SINCE THE LAST BARRIER (a HirStmt::Barrier CLEARS `W_X`; a SharedWrite of X with index `w` appends `w`). For each later SharedRead `S[r]` of the SAME id X (still no intervening HirStmt::Barrier), compute `index_relation(w_k, r) ∈ {ProvablyEqual, ProvablyDisequal, Unknown}` against EACH prior write index `w_k ∈ W_X`, then classify:
  - **ProvablyEqual to ANY `w_k ∈ W_X`** (the read hits a slot this invocation itself wrote earlier in the block — e.g. `tile[0u32]=a; tile[1u32]=b; let w=tile[0u32];` is ProvablyEqual to the `tile[0u32]=a` write) -> **NO diagnostic** (correct same-invocation self-RAW). This is the zero-false-positive guarantee and is checked FIRST.
  - **else, ProvablyDisequal to EVERY `w_k ∈ W_X`** (the read provably hits a slot this invocation NEVER wrote — e.g. `S[local_id]=...; ... = S[bxor(local_id,1u32)]`, or `S[a]` vs a set of distinct constants none equal to `a`) -> **HARD ERROR HirError::SharedMissingBarrierBeforeCrossInvocationRead**. A provably-other slot in the same block with no barrier is the canonical NVIDIA-passes/AMD-races trap, decidably wrong.
  - **else** (Unknown vs at least one prior write — NOT provably equal to any AND NOT provably disequal to all: arithmetic/dynamic index, a LocalRead whose binding was reassigned between the write and the read, or one constant + one variable) -> **ADVISORY HirWarning::SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead** only.
WHY THE r2 MOST-RECENT-ONLY KEY WAS STILL UNSOUND: pairing `r` against only the MOST-RECENT write false-positived a correct multi-slot self-write — `tile[0]=a; tile[1]=b; let w=tile[0];` saw most_recent=IntLit(1) vs read=IntLit(0)=ProvablyDisequal -> HARD ERROR, even though slot 0 WAS written by THIS invocation earlier. Tracking the SET `W_X` (read 0 is ProvablyEqual to the retained `tile[0]=a` write) restores NO-diagnostic for that case. NOTE on the single-invocation case: a `@workgroup(1,1,1)` kernel that writes ONLY S[0] then reads an UNwritten S[1] still HARD-ERRORS (read 1 is ProvablyDisequal to the only member {0} of `W_X`) — this is ACCEPTABLE and intended: S[1] was written by nobody (single invocation), so the read is UNINITIALIZED, buggy regardless of any barrier; the hard error correctly rejects an already-incorrect kernel. Only the diagnostic NAME ('missing barrier before cross-invocation read') is slightly off — the true bug is an uninitialized read — which is cosmetic, not a soundness hole.

`index_relation` is a small, total structural predicate over `HirExpr` (VERIFIED implementable against crates/axc-hir/src/expr.rs):
  - ProvablyEqual iff: both `LocalRead(BindingId)` with the SAME BindingId AND that binding was NOT reassigned (no HirStmt::Assign to it) anywhere between the write and the read (BindingId derives Eq/Hash, expr.rs:20-21); OR both `IntLit` with EQUAL value; OR both `GidBuiltin` with the same axis.
  - ProvablyDisequal iff: both `IntLit` with DISTINCT values; OR both `GidBuiltin` with DISTINCT axes; OR other clearly-constant-distinct leaf forms.
  - Unknown otherwise (any `Binary`/arith index, a reassigned `LocalRead`, mixed constant-vs-variable, or any shape the predicate does not recognise). Unknown is the SAFE default — it never hard-errors.

UNDECIDABLE STRUCTURAL CASES (always advisory, never hard error): write and read in DIFFERENT basic blocks; read loop-carried across a back-edge (the WAR hazard the matmul second barrier protects — spans a back-edge, invisible to the straight-line lint); either behind a divergent branch. Rationale: cross-invocation aliasing through dynamic indices is undecidable in general; only the same-block, no-intervening-barrier, PROVABLE-cross-slot case is a sound hard error. The compiler does NOT auto-insert barriers (dataflow intent unknowable). SOUNDNESS PROPERTY: the hard error fires on NO correct kernel (every provable self-read and every undecidable case is excluded from the error path).

#### A.4.2 OQ2 — divergent barrier = HARD ERROR via a SEPARATE conditional_depth counter (r2 clarification)
WHY A BARE `divergent_context_depth > 0` IS WRONG: the existing single counter divergent_context_depth (typecheck.rs:545) is incremented at if-then (typecheck.rs:956), else (965), AND `while` (1174) — but the doc-comment (typecheck.rs:543-544) confirms for-range does NOT increment it. A bare `divergent_context_depth > 0` check would therefore ALSO flag a barrier inside a uniform `while`-loop body, which A.4.2 says must be PERMITTED (only conditional if/else divergence is UB; a workgroup-uniform loop body is entered by all invocations). It cannot distinguish 'inside an if/else body' from 'inside a while body'.

FIX (the concrete discriminator): add a SEPARATE counter `conditional_depth: u32` to TypeChecker, incremented ONLY around if-then and else bodies (paired with the existing divergent_context_depth increments at typecheck.rs:956 and 965) and NOT around `while` (1174) nor for-range (check_for_stmt at 998 — already increments neither). The divergent-barrier HARD ERROR fires from the workgroup_barrier()/barrier_all() handler in check_builtin_call_stmt (typecheck.rs:2008-2044; the line-2007 comment 'does NOT consult divergent_context_depth — deferred' is UPDATED): if `conditional_depth > 0` at the barrier site -> HARD ERROR HirError::BarrierInDivergentContext (OpControlBarrier in non-uniform flow is UB in Vulkan). A barrier where conditional_depth == 0 (top-level, or inside a for-range / while loop body) is PERMITTED. divergent_context_depth is LEFT UNCHANGED — it continues to gate the subgroup-collective-op warning (typecheck.rs:2089, validate.rs:189); only the NEW conditional_depth gates the barrier error. SAFETY: the shipped matmul/attention K-loops use `for ... in range(...)` (VERIFIED examples/matmul_tile.axc + q4km_dequant_matmul.axc), so conditional_depth (and divergent_context_depth) are 0 at their barrier sites — NEVER flagged. A barrier inside a uniform `while` body is likewise conditional_depth 0 -> ACCEPTED (the half AT-1635 adds).

#### A.4.3 CROSS-VENDOR RACE HONESTY (bounded gap — the most dangerous hole)
A missing/insufficient WorkgroupMemory barrier passes on NVIDIA (subgroup-32 lockstep) AND Lavapipe (serial CPU emulation) but RACES on AMD wave64 / Intel where a workgroup spans independent SIMD groups. Therefore AT-1606 can ONLY prove (i) bit-exactness WITH the barrier present and (ii) that the warning/error fires for the barrier-absent variant. It CANNOT prove the barrier is load-bearing on available hardware. True cross-vendor race validation requires EB.1 (AMD/Intel CI). The REAL protection against a Coder's missing-barrier bug is the OQ1 compiler HARD ERROR (the sound provable-cross-slot same-block case, A.4.1), NOT the test. The barrier semantics are provably correct ON PAPER and verified in subgroup.rs; the empirical race-detection is unavailable in current CI and is labeled an untested gap (EB.1), NOT implied-covered.

### PART B — Competitive tiled matmul (shared-staged + coopmat)

#### B.1 Tiling
For C[M,N]=A[M,K]·B[K,N], each workgroup computes one TILE_M×TILE_N output tile. Across K in TILE_K steps:
1. Workgroup cooperatively loads A[tile_row, k:k+TILE_K] into shared[f16, TILE_M*TILE_K] (a_tile) and B[k:k+TILE_K, tile_col] into shared[f16, TILE_K*TILE_N] (b_tile). Each invocation loads a strided (coalesced) subset from the f16 SSBOs.
2. `workgroup_barrier();` (write-visibility of the staged tiles).
3. coopmat_load A and B tiles FROM the shared arrays via the SHARED-source single-index path (emit_coopmat_load_shared_inline), coopmat_mul_add accumulate into the accumulator coopmat. STRIDE = the shared-tile row width in ELEMENTS (which differs from the SSBO row stride).
4. `workgroup_barrier();` (WAR — before the next K-tile overwrites the shared staging arrays). This second barrier is loop-carried across the back-edge and is NOT caught by the straight-line lint (A.4.1) — it rests on the hand-written kernel + the AT-1620 bit-exact GPU check with K >= 2 TILE_K blocks.
5. After the K loop, coopmat_store the accumulator to C.
For the q4km fusion variant: step 1 DEQUANTIZES Q4_K_M weights (via existing ptr_read_u8/f16_bits_to_f32 builtins) directly into the shared f16 a_tile, then proceeds identically.

#### B.2 coopmat_load/store from shared — SEPARATE single-index emit (CRITICAL-3)
The M2.1 emit_coopmat_load_inline/store_inline build a TWO-index chain `[zero_id, element_offset_id]` (member-0 of the SSBO struct, then array index — buffers.rs:111 wraps the runtime array in OpTypeStruct). A Workgroup shared array has NO wrapping struct -> the shared path MUST use a SINGLE-index chain `[element_offset_id]` against a Workgroup-class elem_ptr_ty. This is a SEPARATE function (emit_coopmat_load_shared_inline / emit_coopmat_store_shared_inline) — NOT the buffer fn with a Workgroup pointer (that would emit a wrong/extra index and spirv-val would reject OR the offset would be miscomputed). HIR: CoopMatBuiltin::Load/Store carry CoopMatLoadSource::{Buffer,Shared}; existing sites = Buffer (byte-identical). The coopmat op itself is storage-class-agnostic (SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix permits a Workgroup pointer operand); only the access-chain pointer TYPE + index ARITY differ. Guards: AT-1613 (Buffer-source byte-identical) + AT-1614 (shared-source single-index arity + Workgroup class).

#### B.3 @strategy holes that are GENUINELY used (the M3.1.5 anti-lesson)
tile_m/tile_n/tile_k holes are resolved by the autotuner via M2.3 source-text substitution BEFORE the parser, so the parser only sees literal N. The holes drive: `@workgroup(?tile_m_x,?tile_n_y,1)`; the shared array sizes (`shared a_tile: shared[f16, <tile_m*tile_k literal>]`); and the K-loop trip count (total_K / tile_k). AT-1622 compiles tile_k=16 vs 32 and asserts the emitted OpTypeArray length constants DIFFER, the K-loop trip count differs, AND a bit-exact GPU result holds for BOTH values (so a larger-array-but-under-iterated inert configuration would produce a WRONG result and fail — size-diff alone is necessary but not sufficient, per the pessimistic note).

#### B.4 Acceptance / honesty
4096×4096 f16 matmul effective-TFLOPS via the resident benchmark (upload-once / dispatch-N / kernel-only timing; A/B/C allocated once — no per-iter staging leak, well under the 50 GB cap at ~96 MiB), compared to a LABELED cuBLAS datasheet ESTIMATE (NOT a same-machine A/B). The reported %-of-cuBLAS is recorded HONESTLY from measurement (no fabricated target). Bank conflicts: shared[f16, TILE*TILE] without padding will bank-conflict (32-bank model) for power-of-two tile widths and may depress the TFLOPS number; the @shared_tile(pad=K) fix is deferred — the honest report should not be surprised by sub-peak numbers attributable to conflicts. Bit-exact (within f16/fp tol) vs CPU reference for a small NON-SYMMETRIC fixture spanning >= 2 TILE_K blocks (catches transpose/stride AND exercises the loop-carried WAR barrier). The coopmat variant graceful-skips on Lavapipe; the matmul_shared_f32.axc f32 variant runs + is bit-exact there (cross-vendor staging proof, but does NOT exercise the shared-source coopmat path — that is NVIDIA-only-tested).

### PART C1 — Correctness-first NON-streaming tiled attention (NOT FlashAttention-2)
tiled_attention.axc: O = softmax(Q·Kᵀ / sqrt(d)) · V. Q/K/V/O f16 buffers; n_heads, seq_len, head_dim scalars. K and V head-dim slabs staged into shared[f16,...] per K-block; the FULL two-pass softmax over the K dimension (accumulate the score row, find row max for numerical stability, exp, sum, normalize) — NO online running-max/denom rescaling. This proves shared K/V tiling + barrier + the attention dataflow. Max-subtraction stays (correct softmax, not the FA2 streaming trick). HONESTY: this is NOT FlashAttention-2 — FA2's defining contribution is the block-streaming ONLINE softmax that AVOIDS materializing the SxS score block (C1 materializes the score row, fine for seq_len=64, does NOT scale to the FA2 regime). The flash_attention_v2 name is reserved for C2/M3.2b. Acceptance: bit-exact within 1e-3 fp tol vs a CPU reference attention (new attention_cpu in benches/common.rs). Runs on Lavapipe (scalar f16->f32 dot products, no coopmat) AND NVIDIA. This is the bit-exact baseline against which C2's streaming softmax will be @equiv_fp_tol-verified.

### PART C2 — DEFERRED to M3.2b (the actual FlashAttention-2)
Block-streaming online softmax (running max m_i, running denominator l_i, output rescale O_i <- O_i*exp(m_old-m_new) + P*V) and the >=80%-of-FA3 TFLOPS number. Rationale in scope_decision. C2 lands as a separate milestone with its own correctness oracle (per-block running-stat invariants + @equiv_fp_tol vs the C1 baseline) and earns the flash_attention_v2 name.

design_md_additions:
## 3.1.14 M3.2 — shared[T,N] workgroup memory + competitive tiled matmul + tiled attention (NOT FlashAttention-2)

M3.2 adds the first NEW LANGUAGE FEATURE since M2.1: `shared[T,N]` workgroup-local memory (FG.6), threaded lexer->parser->HIR->typecheck->codegen->spirv-val->GPU. On top of it: a competitive shared-staged + cooperative-matrix tiled matmul (the dequant->shared-f16-tile->coopmat fusion carried forward from M3.1.5), and a STAGED attention whose correctness-first NON-streaming half (C1, `tiled_attention`) lands here while the FlashAttention-2 streaming-online-softmax half (C2) defers to M3.2b.

### shared[T,N] — syntax, lowering, barrier semantics

Source: a body-level declaration `shared tile: shared[f32, 256];`. The leading `shared` keyword (lexed since M1.2) introduces the declaration; the type `shared[elem, N]` carries a scalar element type and a compile-time **unsuffixed positive integer literal** N (anti-pattern #1: no inference, no const-expr fold in M3.2). A shared array is KERNEL-WIDE workgroup storage shared by all invocations — NOT a parameter, consumes NO descriptor; a shared type in parameter position is a hard error.

Lowering: parser -> `Stmt::SharedDecl` + `TypeRef::Shared(elem,N)`; lower.rs collects each into `KernelBodyTyped.shared` with a monotonic `SharedId`, validating N>0, N<=65536, allowed element type (f32/f16/f64/i8/u8/i32/u32/i64/u64 — Bool rejected), unique name, no param/binding collision, aggregate-bytes limits (warn >16384 portable min, error >65536). typecheck resolves `name[i]`->`SharedRead` (index must be U32, no coercion) and `name[i]=v`->`SharedWrite` (value elem type exact).

SPIR-V codegen (emit_shared_globals, before begin_block, like SSBOs):
```
%elem    = <scalar type>
%n_const = OpConstant %u32 256          ; length is an OpConstant id (SPIR-V 3.32.6), NOT a literal
%arr     = OpTypeArray %elem %n_const   ; SIZED array (not RuntimeArray)
%ptr_wg  = OpTypePointer Workgroup %arr
%var     = OpVariable %ptr_wg Workgroup ; global, no initializer
%ptr_e   = OpTypePointer Workgroup %elem ; shared across arrays of the same elem type
```
Indexed access uses a SINGLE-index access chain `OpAccessChain %ptr_e %var %idx` (contrast the SSBO two-index `%var %0 %idx` — the shared array has no wrapping struct). The Workgroup StorageClass requires **no new capability or extension** (core Shader); f16/i8/i16/i64/f64 elements pull in only the corresponding Float16/Int8/Int16/Int64/Float64 type capability (set explicitly in emit_shared_globals — observe_type does NOT cover F16) — explicitly NOT the StorageBuffer8/16BitAccess KHR storage extensions (those gate the StorageBuffer class only). Workgroup vars are excluded from the SPIR-V 1.3 OpEntryPoint interface list (forward-compat: 1.4+ lists all globals; repo pins 1.3). Two distinct shared arrays of the same elem type get distinct OpTypeArray+OpVariable ids but share the elem-ptr type (dedup must not collapse them). The Workgroup OpVariable is uninitialized (Vulkan forbids initializers without VK_KHR_zero_initialize_workgroup_memory) — reading a never-written cell reads garbage; correctness rests on write-before-read + barrier discipline.

### REQUIRED barrier + memory semantics (the correctness hazard)

A cross-invocation read-after-write through shared memory is correct ONLY with a workgroup control barrier carrying WorkgroupMemory semantics between the write and read phases. AXIOM-Compute reuses `workgroup_barrier()` verbatim (verified in codegen/src/subgroup.rs):
```
OpControlBarrier %Workgroup(2) %Workgroup(2) %(AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory = 0x108)
```
Execution scope Workgroup(2) => all invocations rendezvous; WorkgroupMemory(0x100) => prior shared writes visible to subsequent shared reads across invocations. A single barrier suffices for the straight-line stage->barrier->read pattern; the LOOPED matmul needs TWO barriers per K-iteration (write-visibility + WAR before the next iteration overwrites the staging arrays).

**Missing-barrier policy (sound, SET-based: provably-other slot -> hard error; provable self-read -> no diagnostic; undecidable -> warning).** A barrier is required only for a CROSS-invocation read — one invocation reading a slot a DIFFERENT invocation wrote. An invocation always observes its OWN prior writes in program order, so a same-invocation self read-after-write (`tile[i]=v; ...=tile[i];`, AND the multi-slot `tile[0]=a; tile[1]=b; let w=tile[0];`) needs NO barrier and must never be flagged. The compiler tracks the SET W_X of ALL prior SharedWrite indices to id X in the SAME basic block since the last barrier (a barrier clears the set). For a later SharedRead `S[r]` of X with no intervening barrier and no branch/back-edge: if `r` is PROVABLY EQUAL to ANY prior write index in W_X it emits NO diagnostic (correct self-RAW — the invocation reads a slot it itself wrote); else if `r` is PROVABLY DISEQUAL to EVERY prior write index in W_X (a provably-other slot — distinct constants, or e.g. `S[local_id]` vs `S[bxor(local_id,1)]`, or a read of a never-written slot) it emits a HARD ERROR (`SharedMissingBarrierBeforeCrossInvocationRead`) — the canonical NVIDIA-passes/AMD-races trap, decidable with zero false positives; else (the relation is UNDECIDABLE against at least one prior write — dynamic/arithmetic index, a reassigned binding, or the write and read are in different blocks / loop-carried across a back-edge / behind a divergent branch) it emits only an advisory warning (`SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead`). Provable index equality/disequality is decided structurally (same LocalRead binding with no intervening reassignment, equal IntLit, same/distinct GidBuiltin axis). Pairing against the SET of prior writes (not just the most-recent) is what avoids false-positiving the multi-slot self-write. The hard error fires on NO correct kernel; the one residual case it rejects — a single-invocation kernel reading a slot NOBODY wrote — is an uninitialized read, buggy regardless of any barrier (only the diagnostic name is slightly off). The compiler does NOT auto-insert barriers.

**Divergent-barrier policy (hard error).** `workgroup_barrier()` inside an `if`/`else` body that not all invocations provably enter is UB in Vulkan and is a HARD ERROR (`BarrierInDivergentContext`). A barrier inside a `for-range` or workgroup-uniform `while` loop body (entered by all invocations) is accepted. The distinction is made by a dedicated `conditional_depth` counter that increments ONLY at if-then/else bodies — NOT at while or for-range — so a barrier in a uniform loop body (the matmul/attention K-loop) is correctly permitted while a conditional-branch barrier is rejected. (The pre-existing `divergent_context_depth`, which while DOES increment, continues to gate the separate subgroup-collective-op warning and is left unchanged.)

**Cross-vendor race honesty (bounded gap).** A missing/insufficient WorkgroupMemory barrier passes on NVIDIA (subgroup-32 lockstep) AND on Lavapipe (serial CPU emulation) but RACES on AMD wave64 / Intel where a workgroup spans independent SIMD groups. The barrier-visibility oracle (examples/shared_reduce.axc, AT-1606) therefore proves only (i) bit-exactness WITH the barrier and (ii) that the diagnostic fires for the barrier-absent variant — it CANNOT prove the barrier is load-bearing on any available hardware. The barrier semantics are provably correct on paper and verified in subgroup.rs; the empirical cross-vendor race-detection that would catch a Coder's missing-barrier bug requires AMD/Intel hardware the project does not yet have (EB.1). The REAL in-CI protection is the decidable-case HARD ERROR above, NOT the test. This gap is untested, NOT implied-covered.

### Competitive tiled matmul (shared-staged + coopmat)

Each workgroup computes a TILE_M×TILE_N output tile. Across K in TILE_K steps: cooperatively stage A/B (or DEQUANTIZED Q4_K_M weights) into `shared[f16,...]` tiles -> workgroup_barrier() -> coopmat_load FROM shared -> coopmat_mul_add accumulate -> barrier (WAR) -> next K-tile. After K, coopmat_store the accumulator. The coopmat-from-shared load uses a SEPARATE emit path: a Workgroup shared array is NOT struct-wrapped, so its access chain is SINGLE-index (`%var %offset`) against a Workgroup-class pointer, in contrast to the SSBO TWO-index chain (`%var %0 %offset`). This is a distinct function (`emit_coopmat_load_shared_inline`), leaving the M2.1 Buffer-source coopmat emission byte-identical (`CoopMatLoadSource::Buffer` is the default discriminator). The coopmat op itself is storage-class-agnostic; only the access-chain pointer type and index arity differ. The shared-tile row stride is in ELEMENTS of the shared row (differs from the SSBO row stride). The `@strategy { tile_m, tile_n, tile_k }` holes are GENUINELY used: resolved by M2.3 source-text substitution BEFORE the parser, so different tile_k yields different literal shared-array sizes AND different K-loop bounds AND bit-exact GPU results for both values (AT-1622 — the explicit fix for the M3.1.5 inert-holes mistake; size-diff alone is necessary but not sufficient). Effective-TFLOPS for 4096² is measured via the resident benchmark and compared to a LABELED cuBLAS datasheet ESTIMATE (not a same-machine A/B); un-padded shared tiles may bank-conflict on the 32-bank model, so sub-peak numbers are expected (the @shared_tile(pad=K) fix is deferred). A pure-f32 shared-staged variant runs + is bit-exact on Lavapipe (the coopmat variant graceful-skips there); the f32 variant does NOT exercise the shared-source coopmat path, which is NVIDIA-only-tested.

### Tiled attention — staged (C1 lands as `tiled_attention`; FlashAttention-2 defers to C2)

C1 (lands in M3.2, named `tiled_attention`): a correctness-first NON-streaming attention (examples/tiled_attention.axc) with K/V head-dim tiles staged into shared[f16,...], FULL two-pass softmax over the K dimension (with max-subtraction for numerical stability — that is just correct softmax), bit-exact within @equiv_fp_tol(1e-3) vs a CPU reference attention, on Lavapipe + NVIDIA. **This is the bit-exact baseline; it is NOT FlashAttention-2.** FlashAttention-2's defining contribution is the block-streaming ONLINE softmax (running max m_i, running denominator l_i, output rescaling) that AVOIDS materializing the SxS score block — C1 materializes the score row (fine at seq_len=64, does not scale to the FA2 regime). C2 (DEFERRED to M3.2b, earns the flash_attention_v2 name): the streaming online softmax and the >=80%-of-FA3 TFLOPS aspiration — deferred because its online-rescale arithmetic is a separate high-risk bit-exactness surface that would overrun this milestone stacked on shared[T,N]+matmul, and because C1 first establishes the bit-exact baseline against which C2's streaming optimization is @equiv_fp_tol-verified (the project's anti-reward-hacking discipline).
